decisions: CSharp initializes literal length to0 and uses the canonical find/insert/replace decision. New slots increment length; equal-key replacement preserves length, destroys incoming owned equal keys and old owned values, and keeps the resident key. Every initializer expression is still evaluated.

Literal capacity is preallocated for the initializer upper bound; CSharp explicit capacity proof omits grow paths for Int dictionaries and generic heap literals, preserves stack/inline ownership and keeps ordinary put checks unchanged. Existing over-capacity parser rejection remains unchanged.

SLG bounded literal and all three growable literal callers probe for existing keys but overwrite key/value unconditionally and publish the initializer count. Reuse their existing found flag and owned drop functions: branch key update/insert, drop replaced owners only on update, leave value writes common and publish SSA distinct length. Preserve hash/Eq, controls/mirrors, capacity, storage and value evaluation.

Growable literal slot selection is shared by entry, function-return and control-region paths. All three key writes need a common update/insert join; the shared owner writer must consume the last distinct-length SSA. Bounded literal uses the same owner replacement rule with its inline pointers.

Current CSharp core7 and additional function/control2 all pass before any SLG edit. Owned bounded case balances2 allocations/releases; heap case balances4 because existing take allocates a replacement table. Two prior incorrect test-oracle records remain failed and preserved.
